summary: Tested new Monthly Reconciliation Checklist PDF feature (backend endpoint + Dashboard download button) and dashboard crash-fix regression. Backend: 5/5 pytest cases pass — content-type application/pdf, correct filename, %PDF magic bytes, contains title/TOTAL/legend (verified via pdfminer), zero-activity month returns valid PDF, dashboard.pending_month aligns with checklist default. Frontend: 3 fresh reloads with no runtime error / no console errors / no error overlay — the monthLong(undefined) crash-fix holds. Download button labeled 'August 2026 checklist' (matches dashboard.pending_month=2026-08 from the API — page shows Sep 2026 as current period, previous month is August), clicking issues GET /api/reports/monthly-checklist?month=2026-08 returning 200 application/pdf, triggers browser download 'reconciliation-checklist-2026-08.pdf' (2707 bytes, valid PDF), does not navigate away, no console errors captured.
critical_code_review_comments: reports.py month_label uses map(int, month.split('-')) with no try/except — malformed month query param (e.g. 'foo') would raise ValueError → 500. Consider validating month format at endpoint (regex ^\d{4}-\d{2}$) and returning 400.
server.py monthly_checklist endpoint has no upper bound on Mongo to_list(10000) for cc_transactions/wcdl_loans per facility — fine at current scale but worth noting for future audit.
Dashboard.jsx: downloadChecklist has no in-flight guard — rapid double-clicks fire duplicate downloads (minor UX).
seed_data_creation: None — used existing seeded facilities read-only.
context_for_next_testing_agent: New endpoint GET /api/reports/monthly-checklist?month=YYYY-MM lives in server.py L354; reports.py uses reportlab. Test file /app/backend/tests/test_monthly_checklist.py covers PDF response, filename, zero-activity month, dashboard alignment, and text content via pdfminer. EMPTY dashboard state in App.js now pre-populates pending_certificates:[] and pending_month:<current YYYY-MM> as safe defaults — verified reload cycle produces no monthLong(undefined) crash.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found this iteration.
